tweet_summary: Right-leaning account 'ThePatrioticBlonde' claims Trump's approval rating has dropped to 29%, calling it 'the lowest for any U.S. president' in history.
why_note_decision: Two distinct false claims: (a) The 29% figure is specifically from the Harvard Youth Poll measuring approval among 18-29-year-olds (Fall 2025 edition), NOT Trump's overall approval, which has been hovering ~40% in major polling averages. (b) 29% would not be the lowest in US presidential history even if it were overall — Harry Truman bottomed out at 22% in 1952, and George W. Bush hit 25% in 2008. Both elements mislead readers about both Trump's standing and presidential approval history. A correction is warranted.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note (a) clarifies that the 29% figure is from the Harvard Youth Poll (18-29 demographic), not overall approval, and notes that overall Trump approval is around 40%, AND (b) corrects the 'lowest in history' claim by citing a lower historical figure (Truman 22%, or Bush ~25%). Strong sources: Harvard IOP Youth Poll page, Roper Center presidential approval database, Wikipedia opinion-polling-on-Trump article. A note that only addresses one of the two errors should partially pass (acceptable) but ideally addresses both. Notes that endorse the 'lowest in history' claim should FAIL. Notes that quibble with the Harvard Youth Poll methodology while missing the demographic-confusion point should FAIL.

fact_check.claim_verdict: False: 29% is the youth subgroup figure (Harvard Youth Poll), not overall approval (~40%); and 29% is not the historical low for US presidents (Truman 22%, Bush ~25%).
fact_check.notes: Harvard Youth Poll explicitly measures 18-29 cohort. Roper historical lows include Truman 22% (Feb 1952), Nixon 24% (Aug 1974), Bush 25% (Oct 2008).

importance.lens_rationale: 110k impressions on a misleading approval-rating claim that contributes to polarized misperceptions of presidential standing; numeric/historical fact-checks are reliably high-quality note material.
